meta.source: derived from polymarket.com compiled CSS (inspiration only), roles original
meta.note: P02 D4 extension (2026-09-16): theme blocks, chart arrays, rules. P03 D1 extension (2026-09-17): spacing/border/elevation/density/breakpoints/motion/layers, generated by tools/build-foundations.py — that file is their source of truth, not this one. Brand renamed PolyGM → Openout (see brand/BRAND-KIT.md).

utility.note: P03 D1 additions: the only two letter-spacing values the UI may use, and the loud price size. Emitted as tokens so no component types them.

radius.policy: inherited from the source system (polymarket.com compiled CSS reads `border-radius: calc(0.7rem - 6px)` etc.), kept as deltas so the whole UI re-scales from one base

spacing.rule: every gap/pad/margin in the app is a multiple of 4; 2px and 6px exist only for optical work inside the mark and 1px hairlines

allowed_offgrid.use: hairline borders and the OrderBook depth bar's 1px track
icon-to-label gap inside 11px text, where 4px reads disconnected
stacked yes/no chip gutter at dense density only

chart.note: Adopted arrays are copied from tools/palette-search.py's exhaustive ΔE*ab search output (brand/palette-search.json), NOT hand-picked — a hand-picked list here broke the bar and was caught by tools/p02-gate-check.py G9.
chart.whyNotEightEverywhere: searched per size: dark reaches 8 at worst ΔE*ab 11.3; light's best 6 is 13.4 but a 7th colour drops it to 9.1, so light ships 6 and extends by dash+marker. Note the arrays are searched AT their own size — slicing a bigger result inherits a different optimum.
chart.dashExtension: series 7+ (and light 7+) reuse core hues at a different lightness and are separated by dash pattern + marker shape, never by hue alone
chart.legendText: text.secondary (≥4.5:1) — 3 of 8 dark series hues sit at 3.0-3.9:1, so they are line-safe, not text-safe

never-same-row.reason: outcome.no #D55E00, action.sell and alert.critical all measure ΔE*ab 3.2–4.9 (normal and deuteranopic) against each other — they are effectively one colour. Measured 2026-09-17 by tools/component-colour-audit.py; P02 recorded 4.1/3.2 for the outcome/alert pair only and missed that action.sell IS alert.critical. Layout must separate them: severity renders on the market cell, outcome in the outcome cell, side in the side cell.

rules.outcome-never-green-red: an outcome is a side, not a verdict; green/red are reserved for action and result
rules.colour-never-alone: yes/no carry a word label + fixed L/R slot; profit/loss carry +/−; tape sides carry ▲/▼
rules.below-24px-use: brand/svg/favicon.svg (stroke 6u, dot r 6u — measured 19.4px² per chevron at 16px)
rules.action-buy-aliases-result-profit: same hex by design (ΔE 0.0); disambiguated by slot and sign glyph
rules.no-floats-in-money-path: token hex strings are the only colour truth; UI never renders raw numbers (AGENTS 6)
rules.brand-primary-is-not-body-text: #2e5cff on #0c0e13 measures 3.76:1 — legal only for large/bold UI text and controls; for body-size link text use brand.primary-text (#4e7fff dark = 6.28:1, #1c3fe2 light = 7.35:1). This rule exists because the audit flagged it, not because I assumed it.

hue-is-owned-by-a-column.note: each column may use only its own hue family: the side cell uses action hues, the outcome cell uses outcome hues, the PnL cell uses action hues because PnL is a money direction, not a verdict. Cross-family hue collisions are therefore unreachable by construction, and the audit tool's findings between these two families are expected — they are not defects.

pnl-never-coloured-text.rule: the PnL number is always text.primary. Direction is carried by (a) the +/− glyph, which is mandatory and never omitted, (b) the caret ▲/▼ in a fixed leading slot, and (c) a filled vs outline chip. Colour REINFORCES direction; it never IS direction.
pnl-never-coloured-text.reason: measured ΔL between profit and loss hues is 0.040 (dark) / 0.008 (light) — near-identical luminance, and ΔE*ab drops to 9.0/6.9 under protanopia. A coloured *number* at 11px is unreadable-by-colour for a protanope and its weight channel is useless. A chip gives a large colour area whose ΔL is against the background, not against the sibling, so it survives.
pnl-never-coloured-text.implementation: color: var(--pgm-text-primary); caret glyph coloured via var(--pgm-action-buy)/var(--pgm-action-sell); buy = filled chip, sell = outline chip
pnl-never-coloured-text.open_item: PROPOSED to the brand owner, do not apply unilaterally (P02's palette was approved as a set): a light-theme profit hue with L<=0.10 giving ΔL>=0.12 vs #dc2626 while holding >=4.5:1 on #ffffff, and the same for the dark pair. The candidate #2fd06a reaches ΔL 0.239 / protan ΔE 21.4 / 8.12:1 in dark but only 2.03:1 in light, so no single pair works for both themes; it needs a fresh palette-search run (P02's tools/palette-search.py) before P08 builds any coloured number.
pnl-never-coloured-text.neutral-text-is-exempt: text.primary (and text.secondary) may sit next to ANY hue: it is the absence of chroma, so a low ΔE against a saturated colour means only 'one of these is grey'. Shape, position and words still carry the meaning. Encoded as the `neutral` set in tools/component-colour-audit.py, not as a suppression.
pnl-never-coloured-text.side-cell-shape-code: the side cell is a SHAPE code as well as a hue: BUY is a filled pill, SELL is an outline with a ▼ caret. ΔL between the action hues is 0.040/0.008 and protan ΔE is 9.0/6.9, so two coloured glyphs 20px apart in a dense table must not be the only difference between 'he bought' and 'he sold'.

direction-never-colour-alone.rule: any binary direction signal (profit/loss, buy/sell, up/down) must be distinguishable by shape or position with colour removed
direction-never-colour-alone.reason: measured 2026-09-17: action.buy ↔ action.sell sit at ΔL 0.040 (dark) / 0.008 (light), ΔE*ab 9.0 / 6.9 under protanopia. That is the SAME pair P02 disqualified from the chart palette ('a 7th series drops light separation to 9.1') — so it was already known to be un-separable as a small adjacent swatch, and P02 then went on to use it as the app's directional encoding. Position is not the same as adjacency, which is why it survived the P02 audit.
direction-never-colour-alone.implementation: glyph (mandatory) + shape (fill/outline) + fixed slot; the hue is decoration

no-alert-hue-inside-a-compared-pair.rule: alert.* hues may not be used inside YesNoPair or the book ladder, where the user is comparing two adjacent values; a warning there renders as text.primary + icon + words
no-alert-hue-inside-a-compared-pair.reason: alert.high gold vs outcome.no orange measures ΔE 2.7 under protanopia — a warning would look like a third price
no-alert-hue-inside-a-compared-pair.allowed: standalone badges, the StaleIndicator, toasts, top-bar states

whale-flag-is-a-badge-not-a-dot.rule: the whale flag renders as a chip (tinted background + border + 'WHALE $3.1k' text), never a bare coloured dot beside the side pill
whale-flag-is-a-badge-not-a-dot.reason: alert.critical is the same token as action.sell (#ef4444 / #dc2626), so a critical dot and a SELL pill are literally one colour: ΔE 0.0 in normal vision, 9.0 dark / 6.9 light under protanopia. A badge adds an area and a word, which is also what WCAG 1.4.1 wants here

hue-never-small-text.rule: a semantic hue is text foreground only if it clears 4.5:1 on the specific background it sits on; otherwise the hue is the mark (outline, tint, depth bar, caret, chip edge) and the text is text.primary
hue-never-small-text.measured: outcome.no #D55E00 = 3.87:1 on light bg.base, 3.55:1 on light bg.elevated, 4.26:1 on dark bg.elevated; action.sell #dc2626 4.43:1 and #ef4444 4.38:1 on their elevated panels
hue-never-small-text.why_no_large_exemption: WCAG's large-text bar needs >=18.66px bold or >=24px; the largest text token in typography is 13px (density.font_size_px), so no foreground here may claim AA-large
hue-never-small-text.found_by: tools/component-colour-audit.py graded 3.0-4.5:1 as 'AA-large' and only failed under 3.0, so 11px pill/chip text passed the gate at 3.55:1 while its own size made it body text. Corrected during P03 to grade by a per-cell contrast class (text/large/nontext).

provenance.p02_note: digest of P02's color/semantic/chart/typography/radius/rules; re-pinned 2026-09-17 by P03. ADDED keys: rules.hue-never-small-text. MODIFIED: none — a deliberate strengthening of never-same-row to cover action.sell == alert.critical, which P02's own measurement missed; verified by colour-audit (0 failures), component-colour-audit --gate and p02-gate-check 69/69, and P02 doc line 'the two never-same-row rule' still holds. widths.name: strong
widths.use: focus rings, active tab underline, selected row left rule

widths.name: heavy
widths.use: drop targets (drag an alert onto a market), resize handles

colors.note: border tokens are theme-scoped in P02's semantic block; never hardcode a grey

elevation.policy: a trading terminal is read all day; elevation is used almost never. Depth comes from background steps + hairlines, not shadow.

levels.use: modal, toast, TradeTicket sheet (the ONLY surfaces above 2)

forbidden: inner shadow on inputs (use bg.inset instead)
elevation.light_theme_variant: shadows drop the black alpha to .12 on light; the 1px ring keeps the surface legible instead

setting.storage: user setting, per device, no account needed
setting.why_dense_default: median fill is $5–6 and a 24h book page is 18.4M USD across ~100 markets; a terminal that shows 14 rows is a terminal you scroll

constants.note: min_touch_target 44 is NOT scaled down by dense — dense shrinks text rows, never hit areas; at dense the row's padded box stays ≥44px tall on touch breakpoints. shell-max-width 1680 is the ceiling: past it the user gets bigger gutters, not a 5th column.

values.name: xs
values.layout: single column, one panel at a time, bottom sheet for the ticket, tab bar for Book/Tape/Positions

values.name: sm
values.layout: single column + persistent topbar; ticket becomes an inline panel

values.name: md
values.layout: two columns: chart+book left, tape right

values.name: lg
values.layout: two columns with a rail for watchlist

values.name: xl
values.layout: full terminal: 3 columns (watchlist | market+chart | book+tape), ticket docks right

values.name: 2xl
values.layout: same as xl, wider tape and 12 book levels

values.name: 3xl
values.layout: wide: 4 columns — watchlist rail can collapse to icons, DepthChart gets a second pane (time + price axis), tape shows 24 rows

rules: layout is fluid between breakpoints; only column COUNT changes at them
never introduce a breakpoint above 1680 — a 4k user gets bigger gutters, not a 5th column
the ≥1280 terminal layout and the <640 mobile layout are the only two designs; everything between is a reflow of the terminal

motion.source: skills/emilkowalski-skills/skills/review-animations/STANDARDS.md (Easing + Duration + Physicality sections) — not invented here

easing.decision_order: entering/exiting → ease-out; moving or morphing on screen → ease-in-out; hover/colour → ease; constant motion (marquee, progress) → linear; default → ease-out

micro.use: flash-on-change in, tooltip appear after first

medium.use: dropdowns, selects, disclosure, the tab bar's indicator (a grow-in from the leading edge; a marker that TRAVELS between tabs needs each tab's offset measured at runtime, deferred with the reason in plans/animation-audit.md §P5)

drawer.use: drag-to-dismiss with velocity, ease-drawer — the ONLY surface allowed past 300ms, and only because it is gesture-driven and interruptible (springs keep velocity on reversal)

duration_ms.forbidden: anything animated on a data value: see number_policy

flash_on_change.what: background only — the glyph and the number never move, animate, or crossfade
flash_on_change.why_background: a terminal user tracks a column's vertical position; anything that shifts glyphs or reflows a digit makes the whole column unreadable at 20–30 updates/sec
flash_on_change.ceiling_note: the 300ms ceiling is per-transition; a flash is two sequential ones (90ms spike, 200ms decay) = 290ms total, still under the ceiling both ways. The prompt asked for a 600ms decay, which is over the ceiling per-transition AND in total.

includes: no counting/tweening to a new price
no crossfade between old and new value
no width animation on the cell (tabular-nums + fixed slot keeps layout still)
allowed: a ▲/▼ glyph that changes with the value, not instead of it
number_policy.reduced_motion: flash becomes a 1-frame 1px left border in the same colour, or nothing at all; all transforms become none

mini_app.surfaces: the sheet, the card, the confirm row, the skeleton and the refusal nudge (P12); the desktop dialog panel, its layer and the toast row (P-post, plans/animation-audit.md). The list is the contract and the check reads it: 'no other class animates' was unfalsifiable
mini_app.why_own_token: P03's motion section owns durations and easings; a *distance* has no home there, and inventing one in the webview's CSS makes the promise 'the Mini App is the same design system' unverifiable

physicality.popovers: transform-origin from the trigger (origin-aware animation), never center
physicality.springs: reserve for drag-to-dismiss; bounce 0.1–0.3, e.g. {type:'spring', duration:0.5, bounce:0.2}

vocabulary.note: terms quoted from skills/animation-vocabulary/SKILL.md — use these names in code comments and specs, do not invent synonyms
vocabulary.why_banned: each is a data-integrity risk here: morphing or sharing an element between a market row and a detail view means the same pixels represent two prices at once

rejected_after_review.candidate: stagger-in market cards on the Explore grid
rejected_after_review.verdict: reject — seen on every navigation, adds 200ms to the slowest thing (perception), and the grid is data not marketing
reject — violates number_policy and hides the fact that a number changed

rejected_after_review.candidate: tape row slide-in from the right
rejected_after_review.verdict: reject — 14.7–33.3 fills/sec means 20+ concurrent animations; it also destroys the vertical scan. New rows appear instantly; only background flashes

rejected_after_review.candidate: depth chart path morph on tick
rejected_after_review.verdict: reject — see performance rule; re-rendering a path each tick at 20Hz is the exact way to drop frames on a mid-range Android. New data appends, no interpolation
keep but static opacity, no translate — shimmer is linear motion on a surface that is explicitly telling the user data is NOT arriving
reject — background change only; transform on a row shifts 1px and reads as jitter at 22px height

layers.note: only these 7 values exist; a component that needs a new one is a layout bug, not a token request

components.state_note: the prompt's 8 plus the 3 a terminal needs: stale, disconnected, insufficient — each of which can block an order
